findings.summary: DoD 3's `dispatched_by` is never populated on any production path: `DevelopmentConfig.dispatched_by` is added and threaded to `AgentRunStageActor`, but `cli.py`'s `dd run` construction omits it, no `--dispatched-by` argument exists, and `dd/control_plane.py`'s `LaunchSpec.argv()` emits no such flag despite already carrying `--board-card` provenance -- so every production dd stage run gets the constant fallback `"fleet-graph"`, which duplicates the existing `dispatcher` label and names no 派单主体 (line folder or human subject). The spec required adding the field to the development config chain AND passing it through at create time; only the first half is implemented, so the per-order reconciliation dimension the spec exists to create is still absent in production.

The committed implement handoff records `work_head_commit` as `8cbf440ac2d9b97e1256c50e0daef14a0fca4885`, while the dispatch context supplied to this review states the product commit (`work_head_commit`) is `3d57fd54145993fe5f0eed04616ed90a54312f40` (the implement stage's sealed output). The two are consistent only if `3d57fd54` is the metadata-only materialization stacked on `8cbf440a`; that relationship could not be confirmed with read-only file inspection and is flagged for the chain-verification layer rather than treated as a product defect.

The prescribed mechanical product-consistency check (`git diff --exit-code 3d57fd54 6d92a2e5 -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'`) was not executed: this reviewer has only read-only file inspection and no shell or Git access. Product consistency was instead assessed by direct inspection of the worktree tree and the `.dev-dispatch/` contents, which showed the implement handoff and the RC review artifact present alongside unmodified product sources, with no evidence of a product file altered by materialization. The verdict does not rest on this check.
